newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Singapore's Goh urges S.Africa to become trade hub.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Goh urges S.Africa to become trade hub.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong urged South Africa on Tuesday to take advantage of its geographical position to become a regional hub for travel and trade.

Goh, who met President Nelson Mandela earlier on Tuesday to start a 10-day visit to southern Africa, told a conference attended by cabinet ministers and other leading politicians that South Africa was fortunate to be situated halfway between East Asia and South America.
"South America should not be ignored," he said, adding that capital exporting countries of Southeast Asia could soon start investing there in a big way.
"Here you are between East Asia and South America. You can become a hub for this flow. It won't come in a hurry...but South America is an untapped market," Goh said.

He suggested the first step would be to allow international airlines into South Africa with little or no restrictions. The state carrier might suffer, but the country as a whole would benefit tremendously," Goh said.
"You should look at the granting of air rights as a way of opening air bridges," he said.
